text: Every case has its own icon: 392 hand-drawn glyphs, one per case in Contracts, Civil Procedure and LRS, each a concrete object from the facts, no two alike, in the course colour. Fixes from an independent review of r18 (keyboard start, More menu, phone titles, sync merging).

Study layer: recall drill with staged reveal and keyboard-only sessions, Clean / Patchy / Blank ratings shown on the map and in Progress, confusable pairs drawn from your connections, printable reference sheets, offline install, ratings sync by code, and this version panel. Map: course names and the centre mark keep the same proportions on every screen, the course view always holds the whole course, and subjects open as subtopic tiles listing their entries instead of a bulleted list.
Source links open the original PDFs at the cited page; Supreme Court cases link to their vote breakdown in SCOTUS History; interlocking DKLA mark in the header and at the centre of the map.
SCOTUS History: Court membership by date, seat lineages, and case votes for the Supreme Court decisions in the atlas.
One colour family per course, a single sans type stack, named floor tiles, denser subtopics, sense-tested dictionary links, and the owner's case briefs merged into 53 cases.
Map text rewritten around one label engine (fit or hide, no overlaps), stepped zoom through four levels, and a Wex-only legal dictionary.
Ranked, typo-tolerant search, reporter citations as links, and a print stylesheet for the open entry.
Course layouts designed by doctrine rather than syllabus order, every source claim checked against the files on hand, and the legal dictionary.
The map became the atlas: three course clusters, smooth zoom-and-pan, briefs rewritten from full opinions, and an in-app viewer for source files.
Missing readings added, thirteen new briefs, connection ribbons that survive panning, and a hand-picked icon for every case.
Audit corrections, tapered connection ribbons, doctrine timelines, and plain-language interface copy.
